ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and the integers 7 and 23 are marked near the circumference; a straight line segment connects 7 and 23 and passes through the interior of the circle, indicating that these two positions are at the two ends of the same diameter. Reasoning: The integers 1 to n are arranged in order at equal intervals on the circumference. If two positions are connected by a diameter, then they differ by half a circle on the circle, that is, the label numbers differ by n/2. In the figure, 7 and 23 are located at the two ends of a diameter, so 23 - 7 = 16 = n/2. Therefore n = 32.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing the labels 7 and 23 at opposite ends of a straight diameter of the circle. From the text, the integers 1 through n are placed equally spaced in order around the circle. For equally spaced cyclic labels, two positions joined by a diameter are antipodal, so their label numbers differ by exactly n/2 modulo n. Since 23 - 7 = 16, set n/2 = 16 and solve n = 32.

Using the text statement that the integers are placed equally spaced in numerical order, count the equal gaps from label 7 to label 23 along the ordered direction: 7 to 8, 8 to 9, ..., 22 to 23, which is 23 - 7 = 16 equal gaps. Those 16 gaps make up half the circle, so the full circle has 2 × 16 = 32 equal gaps/positions. Therefore n = 32.
